title: Cash Is Oxygen
briefing: The board wants a liquidity stress test before approving the next growth investment: how long Valtren survives if things go badly at once.
Hollis's team has the data; you design the test and the conclusions.

context.text: The triggers from your first stress test five years ago are still in the treasury policy.
Cash is below 2 million. This test is not academic.

evidence.title: Liquidity position
evidence.body: Cash 4.0m. Undrawn revolving credit facility 5.0m (can be withdrawn if the leverage covenant is breached). Monthly operating outflow 4.4m; inflow 4.6m on normal terms.

evidence.title: Severe but plausible scenario
evidence.body: Top client (14% of revenue) pays 60 days late; a second client fails owing 1.2m; fuel +30% for six months (adds 0.15m a month); the facility is withdrawn in month 3 after a covenant breach.

evidence.title: Actions available
evidence.body: Invoice financing for other receivables (raises about 2.0m within 4 weeks). Defer capital expenditure (0.4m a month). Supplier term extension (about 1.0m one-off).

questions.prompt: In months 1 and 2 of the scenario, before any action, what is Valtren's net monthly cash flow? (Leave out the one-off 1.2m bad debt.)

options.label: About -0.59m a month
options.feedback: Normal surplus +0.2m, less the top client's delayed receipts (14% of 4.6m = 0.64m), less extra fuel 0.15m: 0.2 - 0.64 - 0.15 = -0.59m.

options.label: About +0.2m a month: delayed receipts still arrive, so the usual surplus continues
options.feedback: Cash timing is the whole point of a liquidity test.

options.label: About -4.4m a month: outflows continue while the client's payments stop
options.feedback: That is gross outflow, not net.

options.label: About -1.79m a month, including the client failure
options.feedback: That spreads the one-off 1.2m bad debt into every month.

questions.prompt: What is the most important insight from the scenario?

options.label: The facility relied on for liquidity is withdrawn exactly when needed, so it cannot count in stress
options.feedback: Wrong-way risk: the backstop fails in the same scenario that needs it.

options.label: Total liquidity of 9.0m (4.0m cash plus the 5.0m facility) covers the scenario with room to spare
options.feedback: Counts the facility that the scenario withdraws.

options.label: Fuel is the biggest driver of the cash drain, so fuel hedging is the main lever
options.feedback: It's a contributor, not the key insight.

questions.prompt: What do you recommend before approving the growth investment?

options.label: Set up invoice financing now, renegotiate the covenant with headroom, and phase the investment against a cash buffer
options.feedback: Prepares the levers before the stress and links growth to resilience.

options.label: Invest now: the growth strengthens future cash flow and makes the business more resilient to exactly this kind of shock
options.feedback: Growth funded from the buffer leaves nothing for the downside.

options.label: Cancel the investment until the stress scenario no longer shows a shortfall
options.feedback: Over-reacts: preparation can make it affordable.

questions.prompt: What should the board set as policy?

options.label: A liquidity appetite: at least 3 months' survival in the severe scenario without the facility
options.feedback: A measurable limit that governs future decisions.

options.label: A minimum cash balance of 2.0m at every month end
Leave liquidity to the CFO, who manages it day to day and reports exceptions to the board

questions.prompt: How do you approach the bank about covenant headroom?

options.label: Approach early, share the stress test and buffer, and negotiate before any breach
options.feedback: Banks negotiate generously with prepared borrowers and harshly with surprised ones.

options.label: Raise it only if a breach looks likely, so the bank does not reprice the facility early
options.feedback: Leverage disappears once you need it.

options.label: Tender the facility to other banks to find one with looser covenants

lesson: Liquidity stress must assume the backstop fails when it is needed most. Prepare the levers before the stress and set liquidity appetite as policy.
